subject: Post-demo: SLA windowing & capacity recommendation for Nimbus Retail
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo recap + recommended deployment path

Hi Asha / Miguel —

Thanks for the time today — good conversation and very helpful to see the sample traffic patterns. Quick recap and our recommended next steps so we can align on procurement and SLAs: 

TL;DR recommendation: Start on Hosted (fast onboarding) with dedicated bursts and KV-prefix caching for initial launch (Q1), then move to Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity once Nimbus confirms sustained 120–150 req/s steady-state and 99th-percentile latency target below 120ms under production concurrency. Private (VPC/on-prem) remains an option for later compliance gating.

Why this path?
- Hosted: lowest time-to-value; we can scope a pilot in ~2 weeks. Supports streaming, function-calling, and the eval hooks you asked about.
- Immediate mitigations on Hosted: automatic prefix/KV cache, response streaming, and request-level routing to a lower-latency model variant for hot paths. These reduce p95/p99 tail risk while keeping costs predictable.
- Dedicated: recommended if you need firm throughput guarantees and consistent p99s < 80–100ms at high concurrency; reserved GPUs let you set autoscaling/burst policies and avoid noisy-neighbor effects.

Open items for your side (please confirm):
1) What is the 95th/99th percentile latency target for the customer-facing search experience? You mentioned ~120ms as an internal goal on the call; is that a hard requirement?
2) Expected steady-state RPS during weekday peak (14:00–16:00 local) vs. demo traffic.
3) Any compliance constraints that would push to Private (data residency, audit, KMS/HSM)?

Attached: an initial latency/throughput checklist and a cost worksheet we can tailor to Nimbus traffic (redwood-cost-model-DEAL-4972.xlsx).

Next steps
- If you confirm targets, we’ll size a Dedicated proposal and a Hosted pilot scope with explicit fallbacks.
- Suggest a follow-up 30-minute call next Tue to lock the SLOs and procurement timeline.

Thanks —
Rishi
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — helpful summary. A few clarifications below.

Short answers first: p95 target is 90ms for search suggestions, p99 target is 200ms (hard cap for now). Peak expected steady-state is ~140 req/s for suggestions and ~25 req/s for longer RAG queries. We do have EU customers but data residency is not required today; KMS for keys will be needed.

Questions for you:

Also looping in Miguel (cc) who owns infra sizing. Can we get a short write-up on the Hosted mitigations you mentioned (caching, sticky routing) and an estimate of the p99 delta vs Dedicated at 140 RPS?

Thanks,

Great questions — short answers: 
- Hosted cold-starts: our Hosted control plane maintains warm model workers behind the scenes. Cold starts can still happen for extremely bursty/spiky traffic, but for your pattern (steady 140 RPS) we expect cold-start rate to be negligible after a 5–10 minute warm-up window. KV-cache behavior: initial prefix cache misses cost a handful of tokens for the first few unique prefixes; you can mitigate by priming the cache from client-side warmers (we can provide a small priming script).
- Dedicated warm-up: Dedicated pools keep model instances resident; priming KV and kernel caches typically takes 1–3 minutes depending on sequence lengths.

Attached: a short two-page write-up (nimbus-reqs-latency-throughput.pdf) that explains Hosted mitigations, typical warm-up/priming timelines, and a ballpark p99 difference table. Summary from the doc: at 140 RPS for your mix (70% short suggestions, 30% RAG), Hosted with caching and sticky routing -> estimated p99 ~160–220ms (depends on burstiness and client-side warmers). Dedicated (properly sized with reserved GPUs) -> mid-90s to ~130ms p99 with consistent tail behavior.

I'll attach the short write-up and update the cost sheet for the two paths (pilot Hosted vs 3-node Dedicated reserve) — see attached workbook. Marissa / Priyom: can one of you prepare a 1-page commercial for the Dedicated scenario (pricing + SLA) so we can share with Nimbus?

-Rishi
